summary: Updates some entries in the IANA registry of cryptographic algorithms used by DNSSEC, which signs DNS data. It adjusts how particular algorithm entries are described. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: There is a public list of secret-code methods that the internet's phone book can use. This memo fixes some lines on that list so it matches what people really do.

questions: which dnssec algorithm numbers are reserved
why were dnssec algorithm 4 9 and 11 reserved
subtitle: Three unused DNSSEC algorithm numbers become Reserved, and the registry's references are brought up to date.

tldr.problem: The IANA registry of DNSSEC algorithm numbers had entries 4, 9 and 11 set aside as placeholders for algorithms that were never specified, and older implementations may still use those codes.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes the descriptions of numbers 4, 9 and 11 to Reserved and refreshes the references on some entries.
tldr.outcome: The codes can no longer be handed out for new algorithms, which avoids conflicts with older implementations.

today: RFC 6725 is a Proposed Standard from August 2012. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
DNSSEC uses digital signatures over DNS data to provide source authentication and integrity protection. An IANA registry lists the codes for the signature algorithms, each made of an asymmetric cryptographic algorithm and a one-way hash function.

This document updates entries in the "DNS Security (DNSSEC) Algorithm Numbers" registry. It also brings the references for entries up to date. The auxiliary Diffie-Hellman sub-registries are not altered.
sections.eli5: The internet's phone book signs its entries, and a public list says which signing method has which number. This memo tidies that list.

sections.title: The Changed Entries
sections.content:
Three entries change. The descriptions for assignment numbers 4, 9 and 11 become Reserved.

They were placeholders for algorithms that were not fully specified for use with DNSSEC. Older implementations may still have those codes assigned, so reserving them prevents potential incompatibilities.
sections.eli5: Three seats were saved for guests who never came. Because some old clubs still think those seats are taken, they are marked 'reserved' forever.

sections.title: The Updated Registry Table
sections.content:
The RFC lists the changed rows and states that every other entry is unchanged. Number 1 (RSA/MD5) is shown as deprecated, with a pointer to 5 (RSA/SHA-1). Numbers 15-122 remain unassigned, 123-251 are reserved, and 253 and 254 are the private algorithm entries.

The IANA section says the same: three entries move to Reserved and the reference list is updated.
sections.eli5: The memo shows only the lines that changed and says the rest of the list stays as it was.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document is a registry update and is not meant to be a discussion on algorithm superiority. It states that no new security considerations are raised.
sections.eli5: Only the list is being tidied, so nothing new is risky.
